content.text:
**The upgrade is real, but the “production-grade” and “all simulated shortcuts removed” claims are contradicted by the code. I would block funded payouts and revise the submission claims.**

I verified that GitHub’s latest `main` is [`96da127df488502f364a267311c4a63878a8a4e2`](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/commit/96da127df488502f364a267311c4a63878a8a4e2), and matched 47 reviewed local file hashes against GitHub. Your repository remains unchanged; all execution and reproduction work used an isolated copy.

**Rotate/revoke the exposed LiteLLM and Crustdata credentials immediately**, check their usage logs, and remove them from shared transcripts and walkthroughs. I have not used or reproduced them.

1. **P1 — The restitution policy does not gate claim generation.**  
   `forensicAssessment` is attached to the report, but its `restitutionPolicyTriggered` value never controls replay or manifest creation. I reproduced a `MARKET_VOLATILITY` assessment with restitution explicitly disabled that nevertheless produced a **700 USDC claim manifest** and `COMPLETED` status. Both demo scripts register the resulting manifest without checking that decision. The claimed “halting automated restitution” behavior is absent. [Investigator](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/agent/investigator.ts#L270), [demo registration](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/scripts/run_demo.ts#L116).

2. **P1 — Expiry sweeping can consume another incident’s funding.**  
   Claims reduce the global commitment, but never reduce an incident’s `totalAmount`. Sweeping transfers that original total, including amounts already claimed. My executed contract reproduction funded incidents A and B with 100 tokens each, claimed 40 from A, then swept A. The sweep transferred **100 instead of 60**, leaving only 60 for B’s 100-token entitlement; B’s valid claim reverted. Saturating the commitment counter to zero also conceals accounting violations. Sweeping sets `finalized=false`, allowing the incident ID to be registered again while its old claim flags remain. [Distributor](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/contracts/src/RestitutionDistributor.sol#L106).

3. **P1 — “VERIFIED wrongful liquidation” does not establish oracle causation.**  
   The replay checks baseline solvency, but never requires the borrower to become liquidatable at the faulty price. It does not use `liqEvent.oraclePriceUsed` to establish causation or reject liquidation amounts exceeding the initial position. Using the Base demo’s actual fixture—3 WETH collateral, 3,500 USDC debt, $1,800 price—I reproduced **faulty health factor 1.2343**, yet the engine returned `VERIFIED` and 700 USDC restitution. That position remains healthy under the supplied 80% threshold. Decimal scaling was added, but debt is still treated as worth $1 per token, and the investigator never supplies asset decimals. This supports a narrow stablecoin model, not arbitrary multi-asset restitution. [Replay engine](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/economics/counterfactual.ts#L168).

4. **P1 — Live incident discovery is incompatible with important real-world cases.**  
   Both liquidation events are declared in the ABI, so `pool.filters.Liquidation` always exists; the fallback to `LiquidationCall` is never selected. I confirmed the query uses the demo event topic. Discovery scans the **latest 50 blocks**, rather than an incident-relative window. Oracle and borrower reads use latest state, not historical pre-incident state, so post-liquidation balances can be treated as initial balances. `getAssetPrice` is declared but never called; baseline price and threshold retain defaults. Missing receipts, failed reads, or skipped borrowers can still yield `COMPLETED`. The supposed recovery handler simply returns fixtures without retrying RPC or applying backoff. [Discovery](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/agent/investigator.ts#L163), [position reads](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/agent/investigator.ts#L228).

5. **P1 — LLM failures approve restitution using fabricated certainty.**  
   Structured JSON is requested in the prompt, but no API response schema or `response_format` is supplied. I reproduced malformed output producing `restitutionPolicyTriggered=true`, confidence **0.95**, and `isLiveLlm=true`. Unknown classifications default to faulty oracle; missing confidence defaults to 0.95. Network failure or missing configuration returns a fixed 98.5%-confidence verdict claiming external-feed corroboration that the code never performs. Moreover, assessment happens **before** blockchain collection, using hardcoded $1,800, 10% deviation, and fixture-derived counts. The SDK has a six-second request timeout plus one retry; this does not guarantee a six-second overall investigation bound. [LLM implementation](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/agent/llm.ts#L88).

6. **P1 for submission integrity — The sentinel’s anomaly is scripted.**  
   The third cycle always invents a 10% drop and supplies synthetic liquidation and borrower fixtures, including invalid transaction identifiers. This happens outside demo mode too. The advertised TWAP, liquidation velocity, and mempool monitoring are not implemented, and the “24/7” watcher stops after 100 cycles. The investigator follows a fixed sequence; the model’s recommended workflow does not control tool execution. Calling this autonomous live incident detection materially overstates its behavior. [Sentinel](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/scripts/watch_production_sentinel.ts#L52).

7. **P2 — The Base demo proves sandbox distribution, not historical incident reconstruction.**  
   It forks current Base, deploys a mock USDC token, mints treasury funding, and supplies hardcoded victim balances and liquidation records that bypass discovery. The script does not reconstruct those records from the purported historical transaction or pin the historical block. Chain ID and incident prices in its evidence are hardcoded. A successful run can demonstrate a Merkle claim on a fork, but cannot substantiate the claimed historical forensic analysis. The manifest also incorrectly receives the **distributor address as `payoutToken`**. [Base script](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/scripts/run_base_fork.ts#L89), [manifest construction](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/agent/investigator.ts#L312).

8. **P2 — Health, enrichment, and benchmark claims exceed their implementations.**  
   Health performs a real RPC probe; the other external services are classified by environment-variable presence. Distributor health is unconditional. Crustdata makes **no API request** and labels every address with bytecode a verified MEV bot; failed bytecode reads become retail classifications. The production simulation guard is real and defaults to denying execution, but `ALLOW_PROD_SIMULATION=true` opens it globally without caller authentication or concurrency protection. Benchmark Suite 5 counts file sizes against three manually selected files—it performs no AST/CPG analysis. The benchmark also prints “100% SUCCESS” unconditionally and does not fail its process for failed assertions. [Health](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/app/api/health/route.ts#L29), [enrichment](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/agent/crustdata.ts#L42), [API guard](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/src/app/api/run-simulation/route.ts#L11), [benchmark](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/scripts/benchmark_evmbench.ts#L239).

Verification results: **6/6 existing JavaScript tests, 11/11 existing Solidity tests, and TypeScript checking passed.** The additional sweep reproduction passed by demonstrating the incorrect transfer and subsequent failed valid claim. The production build failed here because Google Fonts could not resolve, so I cannot independently confirm the full release gate. Passing existing tests is credible; those tests omit the central production failure cases above. The upgrade only changed the JavaScript tests’ provider configuration and timeout allowances. [Tests](https://github.com/Proofofaudit/poa-neathack/blob/96da127/tests/investigation.test.ts).

Prioritized next actions:

1. **Immediately:** rotate exposed credentials and block funded use of this version.
2. **Before any payout:** enforce the policy decision, make unavailable or invalid evidence return `NEEDS_REVIEW`, and fix per-incident remaining liabilities and expiry handling.
3. **Before claiming real incident support:** implement one protocol adapter with historical state, correct event selection, incident-bound discovery, asset pricing, and ordered handling of repeated liquidations.
4. **Before submission:** clearly label synthetic sentinel triggers and fork fixtures; replace unsupported “live,” “verified,” “AST,” and “official EVMbench” claims with what the code actually demonstrates.
5. **Then validate:** add negative tests for denied policy decisions, malformed LLM output, missing evidence, healthy-at-faulty-price positions, partial-claim sweeps, and multiple incidents; record a fresh, pinned end-to-end run.

The project has demonstrable arithmetic and Merkle distribution components. Its current evidence supports a **scripted restitution prototype**, while the production safety and autonomous forensics claims need substantial correction.

1. **Fix payout gating and the sweep bug.** These are essential to the project’s purpose.
2. **Make one scenario convincing and reproducible.** Show the evidence, calculation, excluded borrower, and successful claim.
3. **Present the scope honestly:** “a restitution prototype demonstrated on a Base fork.” Label synthetic inputs clearly and explain what remains before deployment.

My assessment: **strong hackathon concept, working core components, significant execution gaps.** Fixing those gaps and delivering a clear, honest demo would make it a much stronger contender. Adding more features should come after that.

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"sed -n '90,125p' src/mcp/server.ts; cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# POA — Proof of Audits

**When an oracle fails, users should not have to prove their losses from scratch.**

POA investigates a disputed oracle update, reconstructs borrower positions, calculates eligible equity loss and produces a funded Merkle compensation package. The demonstration includes a real test-token claim to a recipient holding **zero ETH**, paid for by a forwarding caller.

This is a **hackathon prototype**. Its lending protocol, reference oracle and incident are synthetic. Its receipts, historical reads, integer calculations, Merkle proofs and token transfers are executed on an actual EVM. A Base fork supplies a pinned execution environment; it does not turn the scenario into a historical mainnet incident.

## The demonstration

1. Deploy a lending pool, disputed oracle, independent synthetic reference oracle and test tokens.
2. Seed six borrowers. One is already insolvent before the disputed update; two stay untouched.
3. Change the disputed price from $2,000 to $1,800 and execute four on-chain liquidations.
4. Discover receipts, liquidation logs and historical positions without passing borrower or liquidation fixtures to the investigator.
5. Verify the independent reference, eligibility and reconstructed end balances. Three borrowers qualify for **5,750 test USDC**; the pre-insolvent borrower and untouched positions receive zero.
6. Register the approved manifest, execute a sponsored claim and verify the recipient's token balance increase while their ETH remains zero.
7. Confirm tampered and duplicate claims are rejected and a missing incident receipt withholds the manifest.

The browser displays **saved execution evidence**, including every borrower outcome, anchored blocks, receipts, claim root and policy decision trail. It never invents wallet confirmations.

## Reproduce

Requirements: Node.js 20+, npm, Foundry (`forge`, `anvil`) and Solidity 0.8.24. The Solidity dependencies are checked into `contracts/lib`.

```sh
npm ci
npm run contracts:build
npm run demo:local
npm run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:3000`. The demo starts and stops its own sandbox on an ephemeral local port; it never resets another running node. Each run exports `evidence/run_evidence.json` and `evidence/restitution_manifest.json`.

Full verification:

```sh
npm run verify:release
```

This gate runs TypeScript checking, contract tests (including accounting fuzz cases), policy/API tests, the end-to-end local demo, the project's own Merkle benchmark and the production build. It exits on failure. The benchmark is **not the official EVMbench harness** and makes no academic grading claim.

Pinned Base fork:

```sh
BASE_FORK_BLOCK=<a Base block number> npm run demo:base-fork
```

Without `BASE_FORK_BLOCK`, the runner resolves and records a snapshot before starting the fork. It records the actual chain ID and fork block. An archive-capable Base RPC may be configured using `BASE_RPC_URL`. Failure does not substitute local fixtures or overwrite the last successful evidence with a success claim.

## Safety boundary

- Only the explicit `DEMO_LENDING_V1` adapter can authorize this prototype's manifests.
- Historical baseline state, a successful incident receipt, a bounded log window, reference freshness and reconstructed end-state consistency are required.
- A disputed drop of at least 5% must be corroborated by a separate reference within 1% of baseline. A compensated borrower must cross from healthy to liquidatable.
- Reference or model denial, unavailable evidence, extra position-changing activity, extra oracle updates and repeated liquidations requiring transaction-level analysis withhold the **entire** manifest.
- Defaults cannot silently substitute prices, positions or liquidation events.
- The owner must approve and register a funded root. Model output alone never authorizes treasury spending.
- Per-incident remaining liabilities prevent cross-incident overspending. Sweeps reclaim only unclaimed funds after 180 days. Incident IDs cannot be reused after sweeping.
- Cumulative distribution epochs require funding, nondecreasing aggregate allocation and capped total payouts. Per-beneficiary correctness remains the publisher's responsibility.

The economic policy currently supports single-collateral positions with a **USD-pegged debt asset**. Decimal scaling is not an asset-pricing oracle. Aave/Compound, arbitrary debt assets, multi-asset portfolios and repeated-liquidation causal replay require dedicated adapters and independent validation.

## AI and observability

The default demonstration runs explicit deterministic policy rules without external API calls. `isLiveLlm: false` and the policy name are recorded. No synthetic token usage, market corroboration or confidence about intent is emitted.

Optional live review requires `POA_LLM_ENABLED=true` and fresh OpenAI or LiteLLM credentials. Responses are requested as JSON and validated against a strict schema. Invalid, missing, low-confidence or timed-out requested review withholds restitution. A model may restrict the deterministic policy, but cannot override it.

Neatlogs SDK export is opt-in through `POA_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true`; local trace evidence works without a key. Bytecode enrichment reports contract/EOA-or-undeployed/unknown only. Crustdata company or MEV identity enrichment is **not implemented**.

`npm run sentinel:watch` observes actual Chainlink round changes continuously and reports real deviations as **review alerts**, never fabricated incidents or automatic payouts. Configured demo-oracle monitoring can dispatch the supported investigator on actual `PriceUpdated` events. No mempool or TWAP capability is claimed.

## Production preview

```sh
npm run build
npm start
```

The production UI displays saved evidence by default. Server-side sandbox execution requires both `ALLOW_PROD_SIMULATION=true` and a `POA_DEMO_TOKEN` of at least 32 characters; the browser accepts that access code without persisting it. Input validation, an exclusive run lock and argument-based process execution protect the endpoint. Local development execution requires a matching local origin.

`/api/health` actually probes RPC reachability and chain ID. Optional services explicitly report `NOT_PROBED`; configuration does not masquerade as connectivity. Credential-bearing endpoint URLs are never returned.

## Submission material

- [Three-minute demo and judge Q&A](docs/SUBMISSION_GUIDE.md)
- [Security and deployment boundaries](SECURITY.md)
- [Verification status](docs/BUILD_STATUS.md)

The path to deployment is independent contract auditing, treasury governance, production protocol adapters, finality policies, independent market-reference sources, and operational monitoring. POA does not claim production readiness or guaranteed compensation eligibility outside its supported policy.

# Security boundary

POA is a hackathon prototype, not an audited production compensation system. Use test tokens and isolated sandboxes only.

## Exposed credentials

Credentials pasted into prior task logs must be revoked/rotated at their providers. Editing source code or deleting a transcript does not revoke a key. Review provider usage, billing and access logs, and remove credentials from shared artifacts. Do not commit `.env` files. External model and telemetry calls are now opt-in and disabled in the standard demo.

## Treasury authority

The investigator produces a proposal. The distributor owner registers it. Root correctness, token behavior and treasury governance remain trust assumptions. The distributor verifies membership and limits spending to each incident's remaining budget; it cannot prove an economic claim from a Merkle root alone. Fee-on-transfer and rebasing payout assets are unsupported operationally. Production requires a token allowlist, governance, dispute policy, monitoring and independent audit.

## Evidence scope

The supported adapter reads historical DemoLendingPool state and validates balances and block hashes. Synthetic reference data is labeled. Snapshot evidence is not a transaction-level EVM execution proof or external market TWAP. The current window must contain one disputed oracle update and no unrelated position-changing transactions. Multiple liquidations for one borrower stop the investigation for review. Missing archive state, inconsistent receipts, model denial and stale references never create a payout manifest.

## Server execution

Production sandbox execution is disabled unless explicitly configured and authenticated. The access code must be at least 32 characters. Keep it outside version control, terminate TLS at the deployment boundary and restrict network exposure. Runs are serialized using an exclusive file lock. A crashed host may leave `evidence/.demo.lock`; an operator should remove it only after confirming no demo is running. Demo nodes bind to loopback, use an ephemeral port and are owned by the run; no external node is reset.

## Disclosure

Report a vulnerability privately to the repository owner before publishing exploitable details. Include the affected revision and a minimal reproduction without credentials or real funds.
EOF

# POA submission guide

## One sentence

POA turns an oracle liquidation dispute into an evidence-backed compensation proposal and a verifiable claim—even for a recipient with zero ETH.

## Three-minute demonstration

**0:00–0:25 — Problem.** A liquidation executes immediately. A wronged borrower must then persuade a protocol to reconstruct what happened. POA makes that reconstruction and proposed entitlement inspectable.

**0:25–0:45 — Scope.** Say explicitly: “This is a synthetic lending incident executed on an actual local EVM or a pinned Base fork. It is not a recovered historical exploit.” Show the environment and saved-run timestamp.

**0:45–1:25 — Evidence.** Run the local demo. Show that the investigator receives only contract addresses and the incident transaction—not borrower balances or liquidation fixtures. Open the anchored baseline block, incident receipt and four liquidation events.

**1:25–1:55 — Who qualifies.** Three solvent borrowers crossed the liquidation threshold. The pre-insolvent borrower is excluded, and two untouched borrowers receive zero. The eligible total is 5,750 test USDC. Explain that this is a scoped equity-loss policy, not a claim that every liquidation deserves reimbursement.

**1:55–2:25 — Payment.** Show the registered root, claim receipt and recipient balance increase. The recipient has zero ETH before and after; a forwarding caller pays gas and cannot redirect the leaf's payout.

**2:25–2:45 — Failure is a result.** Show the executed tampered/duplicate claim checks and the missing-receipt safety stop. Explain that invalid model output also withholds the entire manifest.

**2:45–3:00 — Next milestone.** Dedicated production protocol adapters, independent market references, treasury governance and an external contract audit. End with the evidence package, not an unsupported deployment claim.

## Questions to prepare for

**Why AI?** Optional model review can summarize collected evidence and veto ambiguous cases. The current controller, eligibility checks and amounts are deterministic. A model cannot invent balances or authorize a treasury transfer. Do not imply the default demo makes live model calls.

**What is autonomous?** The controller performs evidence collection, bounded read recovery, rule evaluation, replay, consistency checks and proposal generation. The sentinel observes real oracle changes. An owner remains responsible for funding and approving a root. This is bounded automation, not unconstrained treasury control.

**What is novel?** The integration: historical evidence → explicit eligibility → exact equity delta → token-funded claim, with observable safety stops and proof of payment. Present this as a product workflow contribution; do not claim new cryptography or formal causal inference.

**What does Base add?** A pinned execution environment and actual EVM interactions against a fork. The lending scenario remains synthetic. Fork receipts are not public mainnet receipts.

**What about moral hazard?** Pre-insolvent accounts are excluded. Unsupported or ambiguous cases receive no automatic entitlement. A production policy would need independent governance and dispute resolution.

**What is the trust assumption?** The current demo uses a separately deployed synthetic reference oracle, a known demo protocol and an owner-approved root. A production reference feed, root publisher and treasury must be governed and audited independently.

**Does this run official EVMbench?** No. The project has its own regression tests and measured Merkle timings. No competition score, academic endorsement or official security grading is claimed.

## Submission checklist

- Run `npm run verify:release` and keep the actual output.
- Rehearse from a clean checkout with `npm ci`; do not depend on untracked contract artifacts.
- Check the evidence schema, timestamp, block hashes, recipient balances and current source revision.
- Capture a short recording of the actual run and keep JSON evidence as a backup.
- Show the local demo if the public fork provider is unavailable; label the environment honestly.
- Ensure all exposed provider credentials have been rotated. Never display `.env` files.
- Read the event's actual rubric and required sponsor integration rules before submitting. This guide does not assume a particular judging rubric or guarantee a win.

# POA business plan — planning draft for cfo.ai

**Status:** A structural business case with unvalidated financial assumptions. This file is not evidence that cfo.ai has been used. There are no verified customers, revenue, customer interviews or production savings in this repository.

## Customer and buying decision

**Inferred customer:** The risk, security and treasury team of a lending protocol or DAO responding to a disputed oracle event. No named organization has confirmed interest.

**Workflow:** Investigators gather receipts and historical balances; risk reviewers decide which losses qualify; governance approves compensation; a treasury operator publishes a funded entitlement root; affected users receive funds. The proposed product reduces the manual work between evidence gathering and a reviewable payout proposal. It never replaces governance or assumes custody of a production treasury.

**Decision to validate:** Would a protocol pay for an evidence and compensation workflow, and which team owns the budget? Begin with a narrow paid-pilot hypothesis for one protocol adapter, bounded incident size and human approval. No pilot has been sold.

## Three initial use cases

1. **Disputed incident investigation:** Package historical evidence and identify incomplete or contradictory data. Hypothesized value: less investigator time per case. Measure operator hours and time to a review-ready report against the existing workflow.
2. **Compensation proposal preparation:** Compute eligible losses and exclusions, then independently check entitlement amounts and proofs. Hypothesized value: fewer proposal corrections and less review effort. Measure agreement with an independent human assessment; do not equate passing synthetic tests with production error rates.
3. **Verifiable distribution:** Bind a reviewed entitlement to its recipient and fund only supported liabilities. Hypothesized value: less manual reconciliation. Measure reconciliation time and payment discrepancies in a controlled pilot.

## Product and differentiation

POA joins incident evidence, eligibility decisions and a token-bound entitlement manifest in one inspectable package. The prototype demonstrates historical EVM reads, an independent arithmetic check, Merkle proofs, safe withholding and a sponsored test-token claim. Its first adapter is synthetic; production adapters, reference-feed independence, security review and customer discovery are prerequisite investments.

The initial product is a review workflow for protocol teams. Pricing should reflect investigation and support effort rather than a percentage of victim compensation. The financial model below tests subscription hypotheses; none is a quote or validated willingness to pay.

## Financial scenarios — every input is assumed

Currency: USD. Starting cash: $100,000. Reserve $30,000 upfront for security and adapter validation, leaving $70,000. The reserve is a planning allowance, not an audit quote.

| Monthly steady-state input | Conservative | Planning base | Upside |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Customers | 3 | 10 | 25 |
| Subscription per customer | $500 | $1,000 | $1,500 |
| Cases per customer | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| Compute per case | $5 | $10 | $20 |
| Contract review hours per case | 2 | 2 | 3 |
| Contract reviewer hourly cost | $50 | $50 | $50 |
| Fixed infrastructure | $200 | $300 | $600 |
| Payroll | $6,000 | $10,000 | $16,000 |
| Other operating expense | $1,000 | $2,000 | $3,000 |

Reproduce results with `npm run business:model`; `business-assumptions.json` is the input source and `business-model.csv` is the calculated summary.

**Formulas:** Cases = customers × cases per customer. Revenue = customers × monthly subscription. Direct cost = cases × (compute per case + reviewer hours × hourly cost). Gross profit = revenue − direct cost. Operating result = gross profit − infrastructure − payroll − other expense. Burn = max(0, −operating result). Runway = $70,000 ÷ monthly burn when burn is positive. Break-even customers = ceiling(fixed monthly costs ÷ per-customer contribution).

Reviewers are assumed to be contractors separate from payroll. If salaried staff perform reviews, reallocate costs to avoid double counting. Static scenarios exclude growth, churn, sales cycles, taxes and working-capital timing. A non-burning scenario is not proof of sustainable profitability.

## Customer value model — structural, not quantified ROI

Investigator benefit = cases × (current operator hours − pilot operator hours) × loaded hourly cost × adoption rate. All four customer inputs are missing. Subtract subscription, integration and review costs before claiming net savings. Do not count avoided victim losses as product revenue or verified savings.

## Validation and go-to-market

Interview five protocol risk/governance operators about their last compensation proposal, required evidence, elapsed time, manual hours, budget owner and reference-data constraints. Request permission before using a quote. Seek two bounded design partnerships and one paid pilot; these are targets, not existing traction. Expand adapters only after exact historical reproduction and reviewer agreement are established.

Pilot acceptance: one supported historical incident reproduced, no invalid entitlements in an independently labeled test set, human reviewer agrees with every included claim, missing evidence withholds payments, and the team records actual investigation time and infrastructure cost. Production release additionally requires external contract/security review and documented governance controls.

## cfo.ai completion package

Use this plan and the adjacent assumption/CSV files in the actual cfo.ai workspace. Model the three scenarios and export the resulting plan or include a viewable link/screenshot that judges can inspect. Record actual tool output and which assumptions changed after using it. No local file can substitute for that evidence. Account sign-in, card entry or a subscription agreement must be completed by the account owner.
EOF

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > docs/submission/RESEARCH_IMPROVEMENTS.md <<'EOF'
# Online research and implemented improvements — 12 October 2026

## Why this change

The [official neatHack rubric](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon) assigns 30% to completing a substantial agent task, 25% to effective use of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai, and 20% to the demo. Its evidence requirements explicitly ask for failure recovery, before/after runs, inspectable sponsor evidence and public code. This makes a reproducible investigation outcome more useful than another unsupported product claim.

[Anthropic's agent evaluation guidance](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents) distinguishes actual environment outcomes from what an agent says it accomplished and recommends examining execution traces alongside outcomes. We applied that principle to POA's existing real-EVM synthetic protocol.

The [neatlogs human evaluation documentation](https://docs.neatlogs.com/docs/features/evals/human-evaluators) describes evaluations completed within neatlogs. Our local evaluation is separate; it does not turn the email digest's zero completed evaluations into a claimed native evaluation.

## Implemented

- A full-investigation evaluation runs seven controlled scenarios: normal execution, one transient query failure, a provider range limit, a persistent query outage, a missing receipt, an invalid reference and an unsupported protocol.
- An evaluator separate from the investigator verifies exact per-claim allocations, liability, historical discovery, inclusion proofs, linked SDK traces and the intended reason for a safety stop. An unrelated failure cannot pass a negative scenario.
- Mission verdicts distinguish completion, recovery, safe withholding and unexpected outcomes. Failed SDK spans remain errors and remain visible.
- The judge page displays scenario-level outcomes, trace identities, failed span counts and observed duration. The release gate and CI artifact list include the evaluation.
- Grader tests reject tampered proofs, wrong allocations with valid proofs, trace mismatches, unsupported recovery claims, retained payment packages after withholding and unrelated stop reasons.

## Limits

All seven scenarios use one synthetic lending fixture deployed on a local EVM. They do not establish production reliability or historical exploit compatibility. Default execution uses deterministic rules; live model quality remains unverified. Evaluation runs prepare candidate manifests but do not transact payouts; the separate demonstration verifies the sponsored test-token claim.

The October 11 digest covers a different collection of runs. The new evaluation does not diagnose or relabel its eleven failures. Authenticated dashboard access is still needed to inspect those specific executions.

Actual cfo.ai business-plan output, final narrated video, public code updates and genuine community posts remain necessary. No research result or code change guarantees a prize.

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > work/narration.txt <<'EOF'
A liquidation happens in seconds. Proving that an oracle error caused an unfair loss can take much longer. POA gives a protocol risk team an inspectable path from a disputed event to a compensation proposal.

This is a synthetic lending incident on a real EVM, with a separately deployed reference oracle and test tokens. The investigator starts from contract addresses and the incident transaction. It discovers borrowers, reads historical positions, and checks liquidation receipts.

Six borrowers are examined. Three qualify for a total allocation of five thousand seven hundred and fifty test USDC. One was already insolvent, and two were untouched. Independent arithmetic and Merkle proof checks must pass before the proposal can be approved.

A sponsored claim then transfers two thousand five hundred test USDC. The recipient has zero ETH before and after. The proof binds the recipient and amount. Tampered proofs and duplicate claims are rejected. Treasury publication remains an owner decision.

Neatlogs records the actual workflow, including failed historical queries. Here, a transient failure triggers a retry; a provider range limit changes the plan into smaller ranges. We read the persisted traces back from the provider to verify their identities and hierarchy.

The twelve-case economic regression improves from three correct amounts in the pinned old code to twelve in the current implementation. Seven full investigations also test completion, recovery, and safe withholding. These are our synthetic test sets, not estimates of production accuracy.

Optional live model review uses a bounded set of read-only evidence tools. A provider formatting failure exposed a real integration bug. Strict parsing and bounded correction preserve the safety checks. Default reproducible runs use deterministic rules; the model cannot change compensation amounts or send funds.

Entire Graph helped locate the historical query code and identify four affected callers. We retain its actual output and completeness warnings, then verify the relevant tests. This makes the engineering change traceable without claiming complete graph coverage.
